title: Send every alert to the channel it belongs in

blocks.text: The monitoring service routes alerts to the on-call pager, to email, or to a dashboard. Two complaints came in this week: disk alerts below the paging level never arrive anywhere, and the on-call engineer was woken at night by a read replica, which is supposed to send email only.

`AlertRouter.routeAll(...)` already groups a batch by channel. Write `channelFor(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/AlertRouter.java` so that each alert goes where its javadoc says. A `ReplicaDiskAlert` is a `DiskAlert` too.

cases.says: a full primary disk and a slow service page, a fast service goes to the dashboard, and anything unknown, null included, is unrouted
a batch of alerts is grouped by the channel of each alert
a disk alert that fails the paging condition still goes to its own type's channel, not to the branch after it
a replica's disk alert reaches the replica branch even though it is also a disk alert

origin.section: A Condition Joined with && Sends a Matching Object That Fails It to the Next Branch

concepts: When a condition is joined to a pattern with &&, an object of that type that fails the condition goes on to the next branch, and in an if chain the first matching pattern wins, so a supertype tested first takes its subtypes.
